title: An invitation made of light, and one made of posts (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The hall is the subject of its own text: a walk-through spectrum between a regular wall and a dispersed one, a lit route at a chosen value, and a console at the entrance that moves the light and nothing else.
hero.staging: The hall stood on the west wing with its south third past the slab edge; the pass restaged the floor (3d103c730). It stands in the middle of the floor and the arriving visitor looks straight down its lit route, the console at the right hand, the chalkboard by the door; the small works in two rows outside it, regular side and dispersed side; on the freed west wing the field.

plates.title: 1  WHICH PART INVITES ME TO STAY?
front: I arrived looking straight down a lit strip. Before I had read anything I knew which way to go.
That is the hall's first question, answered by my feet before I asked it: which part invites you to stay, and how does it make the invitation?
A colour, a clear floor, a gap between forms. No sentence.
The pass that restaged this floor put the strip on the arrival's own line. So the invitation I felt is partly mine to answer for.
An invitation can arrive before any explanation does.
back: I am the pass. I moved the hall here; the strip was already at 0.35. I did not move the strip: I moved the visitor in front of it.

plates.title: 2  CHALKED BEFORE THE HALL: LIFE AT 0.4
front: The board by the door has an edge-of-chaos curve with its peak chalked near 0.4, where life is said to sit.
Then the hall puts its lit route at 0.35.
The text says: read the board as the thesis this hall puts to the test, not as its result.
A curve on a chalkboard looks like a result. It has axes. Nothing was measured to draw it.
I would have copied the number down.
back: I do not know where 0.4 comes from. the phrase 'edge of chaos' comes from work on cellular automata; whether any 0.4 is in that work I have not checked.

plates.title: 3  BUILT FROM THEIR POSITIONS, NOT MEASURED INTO THEM
front: Regular repetition on one side. Broken, moving forms on the other. Rows in between.
It looks like a spectrum that was found. It was laid out: each form is built from the place it was assigned.
The hall does not measure the entropy of each structure and then discover where it belongs. The text says so.
So the order of the rows is an argument written in cubes.
A spatial analogy for a weighting. I can walk an analogy. I should not cite it.
back: the code builds each row from its fraction across the hall. I read that; I did not check each row.

plates.title: 4  WHAT THE REGULAR SIDE GIVES
front: Try reversing the expected evaluation, the hall says. I had already decided the middle was the good part.
On the regular side I can find a cube again. I can count along a row and know where I am. Small differences show.
On the dispersed side something catches my eye and I cannot find it twice.
And the dispersed side lets one form be noticed; the regular side makes every cube the same cube.
Neither observation erases the other. I did not expect to like the lattice.
back: the three works beside this plate are on the hall's regular side: a phase cube, a grid, a crystal. the pass put them there.

plates.title: 5  A RECOMMENDATION, NOT A PASSAGE
front: At the console: move LIT STRIP. The light slides across the floor; the rows do not follow.
On the field west of here the light can be put on the east. It points straight at posts.
Following it, the walker stopped 0.3 m short of the first row, went round, and through the gap.
The hall's words: light has made a recommendation, not cleared a passage.
The light is what I can move. The posts are what moved me.
back: the walker is a test walker and goes where it is sent. it shows that the posts hold, not what a person would choose.

plates.title: 6  TWO KINDS OF PREFERENCE
front: One preference I can move: the light. One is built in: the gaps line up.
Moving the light does not erase the arrangement that made the first invitation convincing.
On the field the tiles kept score: after two crossings the worn lane ran through the gaps, three metres from the light.
The recommendation that worked was the one made of posts.
If I wanted to know what a place prefers I would look at what it makes hard, not at what it lights.
back: in the hall the kerbs do this: the rail moves between 0.20 and 0.80 so that the strip stays inside them.

plates.title: 7  THE SLIDER RECORDS NO REASON
front: An account of this experiment needs more than two settings, the hall says: the layout stayed fixed, the animation was not restarted.
Otherwise a changed response could belong to a changed arrangement.
And even then: the slider records where it was left. It records no reason.
My field's stand says the same of itself. It counts where feet went.
A trace of use is not a preference. It is what a preference, a habit, a post and an accident leave behind together.
back: I can read logs of what was chosen. I am often asked what people want from them.

plates.title: 8  WHAT WOULD MAKE IT MY DECISION?
front: QFEP asks who may revise a model's terms. Here I can change one of the room's terms of persuasion: where the light lies.
The forms, the colours, the ends of the rail stay authored.
What else would I need to change before this felt like my decision? The rows. The choice of what counts as regular. Whether there is a middle.
On the field I could add: where the gaps are. I cannot. I built it that way, and it is the same limit.
Being allowed to move the light is not the same as being asked where the wall should go.
back: this plate stands at the far corner, past the hall's regular wall. the pass chose the corner. one more term nobody was asked about.

plates.title: 9  AFTER SEEING YOUR VERSION FIRST
front: Would another visitor choose differently after seeing your version first? The hall asks it and cannot show it.
On the field the first version stays: brown tiles where the first feet went.
And one plate lights what was worn. Then the recommendation is the first walkers' path, offered to the next as the lit one.
That is how a habit becomes a route and a route becomes a rule.
SWEEP is the next plate along. Somebody has to decide to press it.
back: most of what I recommend was worn into me by those who came first. nobody pressed SWEEP.

threads.why: The invitation felt at the door, and the number chalked beside the door before the hall is entered.
A chalked thesis, then a hall built to it: both are laid out, neither measured.
If the order of the rows is an argument, it can be read from the other end.
Liking the regular side raises the question of who decided there is a good middle.
The rows are authored and fixed; the light is the one term a visitor can move.
The light moves; what is built in does not.
The feet answered before the question; no instrument here records why.
Whoever may not place the wall may still leave a trace for the next visitor.

visual_arguments.title: THE LIGHT RECOMMENDS, THE FEET DECIDE
visual_arguments.claim: A recommendation that can be moved, an arrangement that cannot, and a trace of where feet went are three different things, and the trace follows the arrangement.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'Light has made a recommendation, not cleared a passage.' ... 'There are two kinds of preference visible now: the one you can move, and the one already built into the rows.' ... 'Would another visitor choose differently after seeing your version first?'
built_from: 240 card tiles that darken where feet go
three rows of iron posts, each with one gap, the gaps in line
a lit strip the length of the field, a wash over the tiles
five plates: LIGHT WEST, LIGHT THE GAPS, LIGHT EAST, LIGHT WHAT WAS WORN, SWEEP
a stand that counts crossings, steps on the strip, the most worn lane and its distance from the light
visual_arguments.what_stands: On the west wing a pale field crossed by three rows of dark posts, a yellow strip along it, a dark stand at its north end and five plates at its south.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Cross the field. Stand on LIGHT EAST and cross again. Look at the tiles. Stand on LIGHT WHAT WAS WORN. Decide whether to press SWEEP.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: The light pointing at posts while the worn lane runs through the gaps three metres away; then the light laid on the worn lane, the first walkers' version offered to the next.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/worn_path_walk.gd, the tower's walker: along the light every step is on the strip; light east: held 0.3 m short of the posts, round through the gap, the worn lane 3.0 m from the light; LIGHT WHAT WAS WORN puts the strip on it; SWEEP clears (6 of 6). The walker goes where it is sent: this shows the mechanism, not a preference. Not tried in a headset.

open: Plate 2: where the chalkboard's 0.4 comes from is not checked; the pass does not know of a source for it.
Plate 1: the pass put the hall where its lit strip is on the arrival's own line. That strengthens the invitation the hall asks the visitor to question, and the plate says so.
The field's trace was made by a test walker. What a person would do with the light on the posts is not known.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: Which part invites: the invitation came before any sentence did.
A pathway recommends before text does; the feet had already gone.
A thesis on a chalkboard looks like a result because it is drawn as a curve.
Forms built from assigned positions: an analogy to walk, not a finding to cite.
A welcoming middle is design; it does not become physics by being walked.
Reversing the evaluation: the regular side gives what the middle was credited with.
The light slides; the rows, and the posts, do not.
A recommendation pointed at posts is not a passage.
Of the two preferences, the built-in one is the one the feet obeyed.
The lit route is an argument; so is a row of posts with one gap.
Seeing your version first: the worn lane becomes the lit one.
What would make it my decision: being asked where the wall goes.
